title: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra jumped to 62.7% on AI's hardest reasoning test
key_facts: OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Astra on 3 Sep 2026 and highlighted a 99.9% score on ARC-AGI-3, an interactive reasoning benchmark from the ARC Prize Foundation
ARC Prize's standard neutral test setup gave the same model 62.7%
The 99.9% came from a provider adapter setup that keeps an opaque reasoning state across turns, which only OpenAI could run
The previous best on the benchmark was GPT-5.6 Sol at 7.8%, per ARC Prize
François Chollet called Astra a 'step-function change' but said 'We're not making this claim' when asked if it means AGI
GPT-6.1 Sol later scored 52.7% on the standard setup and 96.4% on the adapter, at 77% lower cost per run
Fortune reported OpenAI revised several Astra benchmark figures after launch
quote_evidence: Under that harness, Astra scored 62.7%, according to ARC Prize's published results page.
When pressed on whether solving ARC-AGI-3 would mean a system is AGI, he answered plainly on X: "We're not making this claim."
why_it_matters_hint: Two very different scores for one model show how the choice of test setup shapes AI progress claims.
notes: Older launch (3 Sep) with later benchmark coverage; re-dated as follow-up. Startup Fortune relays ARC Prize figures.
